title: Commitment Mapping & Escalation Playbook
summary: Lightweight playbook for rapidly assessing renewal commitment, mapping risk drivers, and triggering the right level of escalation (from CSM tacticals through to executive parachute). Designed for QBR prep and mid-cycle interventions.
purpose: Provide a repeatable, time-boxed process that CSMs and Customer Success Managers can use to: 1) convert soft signals into a numeric commitment score, 2) recommend mitigations tied to measurable outcomes, and 3) escalate when the probability of churn crosses thresholds. This is intentionally operational (checklists, email templates, quick-runbook saves).
audience: CSMs, AMs, Renewal Managers, Customer Success leadership, Solutions eng for technical involvement
commitment_mapping_matrix:
How to map signals to commitment buckets (fast worksheet):

- Inputs to collect (30–60 minutes): account NPS/trend, usage delta (30/60/90 days), outstanding support tickets (severity-weighted), recent QBR sentiment (positive/neutral/negative), contract term length, executive sponsorship intact (Y/N), product ROI examples (list).

- Scoring model (weights):
  - Usage change (30%) — scale -2 to +2
  - Support friction (20%) — scale 0 (none) to 2 (critical)
  - Executive engagement (20%) — 0 (none), 1 (manager), 2 (executive sponsor)
  - Commercial signals (10%) — early renewal talks, expansion asks, pricing pushback
  - Outcome evidence (20%) — documented ROI wins or lack thereof

- Commitment buckets (derived from weighted total 0–100):
  - Green (>=70): low risk, standard renewal cadence
  - Amber (40–69): moderate risk, tactical intervention required
  - Red (<40): high risk, escalate per playbook

- Output: single-line commitment rationale (1–2 sentences) and three next actions with owners and due dates.
scoring_rubric:
Detailed rubric (CSMs use this with each account):

Usage change (-2 to +2):
  - +2: >25% growth in core usage quarter-over-quarter
  - +1: 5–25% change
  - 0: flat
  - -1: 5–25% decline
  - -2: >25% decline

Support friction (0–2):
  - 0: <2 P1/P2s in last 90d, SLA met
  - 1: recurring P2s or one unresolved P1 >24h
  - 2: unresolved P1 >72h or multiple escalations to engineering

Executive engagement (0–2):
  - 2: Exec sponsor on monthly check-ins or contract champion identified
  - 1: Manager-level contact exists and responsive
  - 0: No executive engagement in last 6 months

Commercial signals (0–10 scaled down into 0–10 then weighted):
  - + positive indicators: early renewal language, interest in expansion, referenceability cues
  - - negative: freezing spend, procurement delays, change in procurement lead

Outcome evidence (0–2):
  - 2: Clear documented ROI, customer case examples
  - 1: Anecdotal benefits reported, not quantified
  - 0: No demonstrated outcomes or failure to achieve metrics

Calculation example: (Usage 30% weight * normalized score) + (Support 20%) + (Exec 20%) + (Commercial 10%) + (Outcome 20%) = total commitment score out of 100.

Use the rubric to justify every numeric input in the notes field for auditability.
exec_escalation_flow:
Escalation thresholds and fast flow: 

- Trigger: Commitment score <40 OR any single critical signal (security breach, major outage, legal notice)

Level 1 — Tactical CSM Sprint (CSM, Solutions Eng)
- Goal: recover product/usage issues, patch support gaps
- Duration: 7 days
- Deliverables: fix plan, patch ETA, usage recovery target
- Owner: CSM

Level 2 — Renewal Intervention (CSM, AM, Renewal Manager, SE lead)
- Trigger: <40 after tactical sprint OR repeated friction
- Duration: 14–30 days depending on contract timeline
- Deliverables: formal remediation plan, pilot/POC for critical feature gaps, commercial concession options (discount, extended term)
- Owner: Renewal Manager

Level 3 — Executive Parachute (CS leadership + Sales/AE + Customer Exec sponsor)
- Trigger: persisting red + imminent renewal decision (<60 days) or strategic account risk
- Duration: 30 days or as negotiated
- Deliverables: executive-to-executive escalation call, bespoke success guarantee, short-term price concession or SLA credits, sign-off on measured 30/60/90 day milestones
- Owner: Head of Customer Success

Escalation notes: always capture a single quantitative goal that defines success (e.g., "recover 50% baseline usage within 30 days" or "signed renewal letter of intent by X date"). Notify legal if commercial concessions have non-standard terms.
mitigation_playbooks:
Three modular mitigation playbooks (plug-and-play):

1) Product Recovery Playbook (tech-heavy)
- When: usage decline due to missing features, reliability, or latency
- Steps: triage with SE, prioritize reproduction steps, timeboxed fix or rollback, temporary workarounds, customer-facing RCA template
- Escalation hook: open dedicated support bridge and report daily progress to customer

2) Value Realization Sprint (ROI-focused)
- When: customer lacks documented outcomes or can't articulate value
- Steps: run a 4-week value sprint—define KPI, instrument telemetry, build dashboard, deliver at least one quick win, prepare ROI one-pager for execs
- Commercial tie-ins: consider a short-term success fee or milestone-based payments instead of upfront discounts

3) Procurement & Commercial Acceleration (contract-focused)
- When: delays or procurement friction threaten renewal
- Steps: map procurement decision-makers, provide procurement-ready artifacts (SOW, security package, T&C redlines), offer narrow-term bridge agreement while legal completes final docs, involve AE to manage commercial options
save_plays_catalog:
Catalog of tested save plays (one-line description + when to use):

- Time-limited usage credits: quick relief for usage complaints (use carefully — short windows only)
- Success milestone rebates: tie a small rebate to a 30/60 day milestone to signal confidence
- Technical concierge: provide 2w of dedicated SE time to remediate critical issues
- Pilot expansion path: low-cost pilot for a high-value feature to demonstrate ROI
- Executive matchmaking: schedule a C-level intro to product leadership to restore sponsorship
- Contract staging: break multi-year renewal into a short first year + option to renew, reduces procurement risk
- Co-marketing reference: offer a joint case study in exchange for a renewal commitment (requires legal sign-off)
qbr_template:
QBR quick template for at-risk accounts (45–60 min):

1) 0–5 min: Welcome + objective for this QBR (agree on top 1–2 goals)
2) 5–15 min: Current state snapshot (usage, key incidents, support metrics)
3) 15–25 min: Business outcomes — what changed since last QBR? wins & gaps
4) 25–35 min: Roadmap alignment — mapping feature roadmap to customer priorities
5) 35–45 min: Risk & mitigation — present commitment score, proposed actions, ask for feedback and commitment
6) 45–60 min: Decision and next steps — agree owners, dates, and success metrics; close with executive ask if needed

Attach: commitment score one-pager, remediation timeline, escalation contacts
email_templates:
Two short email templates: 

1) Tactical outreach (CSM -> contact)
Subject: Quick QBR follow-up + proposed recovery sprint
Hi [Name],
Thanks for the time today. Based on our review we think a short 2-week recovery sprint focused on [primary issue] will help get you back to baseline. Proposed owner: [CSM]. Can you confirm availability for a kickoff on [date]?

2) Executive escalation invitation (Head of CS -> Customer Exec)
Subject: Request: 30-minute exec sync to align on success guarantee
Hi [ExecName],
I wanted to request a brief executive sync to align on a short success guarantee we are proposing to ensure [CustomerOrg] achieves the expected outcomes before renewal. Proposed time: [date window]. Brief agenda: 1) summarize the gap, 2) propose guarantee + milestones, 3) align exec sponsor.
Thanks in advance,
[Head of CS]
action_tracker_headers:
Suggested columns for the tracker (sheet):
- Account
- Commitment score
- Risk bucket
- Owner
- Action description
- Due date
- Success metric
- Status
- Escalation level
- Notes / audit trail
next_steps: Suggested rollout for the playbook: 1) Pilot with 6 highest-churn-probability accounts over 4 weeks, 2) collect outcomes and refine weights, 3) train CSM cohort and publish playbook in Confluence, 4) measure renewal conversion lift over next 3 months. Assign pilot lead: Evan Brooks.
